coverage.note: Six queued articles read. Three named no address: two on the city's $9M settlement over the Alice Griffith housing complex, which is named but never given a street number, and a photo column. A sixth, an arrest story, could not be read — missionlocal.org answered HTTP 429 and read.py has no syndicated copy — and is declined on its headline regardless: a criminal charge against a named individual is a story about a person, and the root AGENTS.md forbids a page from carrying the name. It is not worth a retry. The two addressed stories are declined below.

findings.description: A citywide feature on broken elevators in San Francisco buildings uses a Tenderloin building at 545 O'Farrell Street, without a working elevator for over three years, as one of its examples, in a photo caption. The residents quoted are private individuals and are not recorded here.

citation.label: Mission Local, “‘It’s called being in prison:’ San Francisco has a broken-elevator problem,” 27 August 2026

raw.text: for 545 O'Farrell St., a Tenderloin building that has not had a working elevator in over three years

publish.note: The subject is the city's elevator problem, not this building; the address appears in a photo caption as one illustration of it. The headline is what a page would carry, and it says nothing about 545 O'Farrell Street — a reader meeting it on that timeline in ten years would learn nothing about the building. read.py surfaced this as a hit on 57 Taylor, an unrelated number elsewhere in the text.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 545 OFARRELL ST → parcel 0323023; sf-parcels has blklot 0323023 active, 545–545 OFARRELL; the 2025 roll records it as multi-family residential, built 1910.
